findings.title: Default CA load can prevent Requests import
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize and cache the default SSL context lazily on the first verified HTTPS request, with thread-safe one-time initialization, so loading the CA bundle remains on the request path.
findings.why_it_matters: Because adapters is imported by requests.sessions and requests imports sessions from its public package initializer, this CA load runs during every `import requests`. If the default bundle is missing, unreadable, malformed, or unavailable through packaged-path extraction, that import fails before callers can use HTTP, verify=False, or a custom CA path. It also adds synchronous bundle I/O to imports that never make a verified HTTPS request.
evidence: src/requests/__init__.py:160 imports .api and :174 imports .sessions; src/requests/sessions.py:15 imports HTTPAdapter from .adapters
src/requests/adapters.py:297-317 previously deferred default CA resolution and existence validation to cert_verify() for verified HTTPS requests

testing_gaps: Add focused regression coverage that ordinary verify=True requests reuse the preloaded context while verify=False and custom trust remain isolated, and that the changed CA-directory branch works. Existing tests exercise verify=False and CA files but do not directly assert context reuse or cover CA directories (tests/test_requests.py:2833-2862, 2897-2927).
Exercise default CA bundle extraction/loading in a packaged or zipapp-style install; this import-time path now depends on the extracted bundle being available.
